arxiv-2011-07102.title: The Elastic Properties and Lattice Dynamics for Selected 211 MAX Phases: A DFT Study
arxiv-2011-07102.creator: G. K. Arusei ∗, M. Chepkoech, G. O. Amolo, N. Makau
arxiv-2011-07102.description: Abstract The elastic properties and lattice dynamics of Ti 2 AlC, Ti 2 AlN, Ti 2 GaC, Ti 2 GaN, Ti 2 PbC, Ti 2 CdC and Ti 2 SnC have been investigated using the density functional theory within the generalized gradient approximations as expressed in Quantum Espresso and VASP codes.

arxiv-2301-00419.creator: Wenpin Tang, Hung Vinh Tran, Yuming Paul Zhang
arxiv-2301-00419.description: Abstract . This paper is concerned with the convergence rate of policy iteration for (deterministic) optimal control problems in continuous time. To overcome the problem of ill-posedness due to lack of regularity, we consider a semi-discrete scheme by adding a viscosity term via finite differences in space.

arxiv-2302-03259.title: Relativity and decoherence of spacetime superpositions
arxiv-2302-03259.creator: Joshua Foo, Robert B. Mann, Magdalena Zych
arxiv-2302-03259.description: Abstract It is univocally anticipated that in a theory of quantum gravity, there exist quantum superpositions of semiclassical states of spacetime geometry. Such states could arise for example, from a source mass in a superposition of spatial configurations. In this paper we introduce a framework for describing such “quantum superpositions of spacetime states.

arxiv-2311-18264.title: Cm 15+ and Bk 16+ ion clocks with enhanced sensitivity to new physics
arxiv-2311-18264.creator: V. A. Dzuba and V. V. Flambaum
arxiv-2311-18264.description: Abstract We perform calculations of electronic structure of Cm 15+ and Bk 16+ ions and demonstrate that they have transitions which combine the features of atomic optical clocks with the enhanced sensitivity to the variations of the fine structure constant α \alpha .

arxiv-2402-09966.title: Textual Localization: Decomposing Multi-concept Images for Subject-Driven Text-to-Image Generation
arxiv-2402-09966.creator: Junjie Shentu, Matthew Watson, Noura Al Moubayed
arxiv-2402-09966.description: Abstract Subject-driven text-to-image diffusion models empower users to tailor the model to new concepts absent in the pre-training dataset using a few sample images. However, prevalent subject-driven models primarily rely on single-concept input images, facing challenges in specifying the target concept when dealing with multi-concept input images.

arxiv-2407-02957.title: Past, Present, and Future: A Survey of The Evolution of Affective Robotics For Well-being
arxiv-2407-02957.creator: Micol Spitale, Minja Axelsson, Sooyeon Jeong, Paige Tuttösí, Caitlin A. Stamatis, Guy Laban, Angelica Lim, Hatice Gunes
arxiv-2407-02957.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Micol Spitale, Minja Axelsson, Sooyeon Jeong, Paige Tuttösí, Caitlin A. Stamatis, Guy Laban, Angelica Lim, Hatice Gunes. Recent research in affective robots has recognized their potential in supporting human well-being. Due to rapidly developing affective and artificial intelligence technologies, this field of research has undergone explosive expansion and advancement in recent years. In order to develop a deeper understanding of recent advancements, we present a systematic review of the past 10 years of research in affective robotics for wellbeing.

arxiv-2412-03673.title: Interpreting Transformers for Jet Tagging
arxiv-2412-03673.creator: Aaron Wang, Abhijith Gandrakota, Jennifer Ngadiuba, Vivekanand Sahu, Priyansh Bhatnagar, Elham E Khoda, Javier Duarte
arxiv-2412-03673.description: Abstract Machine learning (ML) algorithms, particularly attention-based transformer models, have become indispensable for analyzing the vast data generated by particle physics experiments like ATLAS and CMS at the CERN LHC. Particle Transformer (ParT), a state-of-the-art model, leverages particle-level attention to improve jet-tagging tasks, which are critical for identifying particles resulting from proton collisions.

pmc-10593964.title: Middle meningeal artery embolization for chronic subdural hematoma: a systematic review
pmc-10593964.creator: Yoshihiro Omura, Taichi Ishiguro
pmc-10593964.description: BackgroundChronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) is one of the most common diseases in neurosurgery. Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) is reportedly an option to prevent recurrence or avoid surgery in patients with cSDH. This study was performed to review the evidence on MMAE for cSDH and evaluate its safety, efficacy, indications, and feasibility.

pmc-10604198.title: The Variation of Electrical Pulse Duration Elicits Reliable Network-Mediated Responses of Retinal Ganglion Cells in Normal, Not in Degenerate Primate Retinas
pmc-10604198.creator: Seongkwang Cha, Jungryul Ahn, Seong-Woo Kim, Kwang-Eon Choi, Yongseok Yoo, Heejong Eom, Donggwan Shin, Yong Sook Goo
pmc-10604198.description: This study aims to investigate the efficacy of electrical stimulation by comparing network-mediated RGC responses in normal and degenerate retinas using a N-methyl-N-nitrosourea (MNU)-induced non-human primate (NHPs) retinitis pigmentosa (RP) model. Adult cynomolgus monkeys were used for normal and outer retinal degeneration (RD) induced by MNU.

pmc-12770880.title: Systemic immune-inflammation index prior to postoperative radiotherapy as a tool for outcome prediction in thymic epithelial tumors
pmc-12770880.creator: Alper Kahvecioglu, Mervenur Bay, Pervin Hurmuz, Mustafa Cengiz
pmc-12770880.description: PurposeThe systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a prognostic biomarker in various solid tumors. However, the prognostic role of SII in thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) receiving adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) has not yet been explored. This study aims to assess the prognostic role of pre-RT SII in TET patients undergoing adjuvant RT.

pmc-13222171.creator: Ian W. Campbell, Kerstin M. G. Brand, Ulrike Gottwald-Hostalek, Julian Dettenbach
pmc-13222171.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Metformin is a safe and effective glucose-lowering agent, widely regarded as the first-line treatment option for type 2 diabetes (T2D), and available at very low cost. Recent updates to the American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care guidance demonstrate a shift towards the earlier use of newer, more expensive, anti-diabetic agents for the treatment of T2D, based on concurrent conditions such as cardiovascular and/or renal complication reduction, and significant weight loss.
